                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`/home/user/catalog` holds an empty Elixir/Mix project for the OTP application `:catalog`. Every dependency it will ever need is already fetched and compiled for both the `dev` and `test` Mix environments (Ash 3.x, `ash_json_api` 1.7.x, `open_api_spex`, `plug`, `bandit`, `jason`, `picosat_elixir`). The machine has **no network access**: do not add, remove, upgrade or re-resolve dependencies, and do not edit `mix.exs` or `mix.lock`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'You must turn this empty project into a book-catalog service that publishes its whole domain as a JSON:API over HTTP, served by the application itself, backed entirely by an in-memory Ash data layer (there is no database in this environment).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Domain model\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Define the Ash domain `Catalog.Library` (`otp_app: :catalog`) with exactly three resources, all using an in-memory data layer:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'| Module                   | JSON:API `type` | Attributes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Relationships                                                |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| ------------------------ | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `Catalog.Library.Author` | `"author"`      | `id` (uuid primary key), `name` (string, required, non-empty), `country` (string, optional)                                                                                                                                                   | `books` — many `Book`                                        |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `Catalog.Library.Book`   | `"book"`        | `id` (uuid primary key), `title` (string, required, non-empty), `shelf` (string, required, non-empty), `year` (integer, required, 1450..2100), `price_cents` (integer, required, >= 0), `restricted` (boolean, required, defaults to `false`) | `author` — one `Author`, required; `reviews` — many `Review` |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `Catalog.Library.Review` | `"review"`      | `id` (uuid primary key), `rating` (integer, required, 1..5), `body` (string, optional)                                                                                                                                                        | `book` — one `Book`, required                                |\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'A record written through the API must remain readable by every later request for as long as the node is up.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### HTTP surface\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Starting the `:catalog` application must start an HTTP server bound to `127.0.0.1` on TCP port `4001`; `mix run --no-halt` inside the project directory must therefore serve the API. Every JSON:API route lives under the URL prefix `/api/json`, so the base URL is `http://127.0.0.1:4001/api/json`. Routes below are written relative to that base URL.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'| Method | Path                               | Purpose                                                 |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| ------ | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| GET    | `/authors`                         | list authors                                            |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| POST   | `/authors`                         | create an author                                        |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| GET    | `/authors/:id`                     | fetch one author                                        |\n'[39m +
                [32m"| GET    | `/authors/:id/books`               | the author's books, as full resource objects            |\n"[39m +
                [32m"| GET    | `/authors/:id/relationships/books` | the author's books, as resource identifier objects only |\n"[39m +
                [32m'| GET    | `/books`                           | list books                                              |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| POST   | `/books`                           | create a book                                           |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| GET    | `/books/:id`                       | fetch one book                                          |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| PATCH  | `/books/:id`                       | update a book                                           |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| DELETE | `/books/:id`                       | delete a book                                           |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| GET    | `/reviews/:id`                     | fetch one review                                        |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| POST   | `/reviews`                         | create a review                                         |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| GET    | `/reports/shelf_summary`           | a non-CRUD report (see below)                           |\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Document shape\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Every response — success or failure — must carry the `Content-Type` header `application/vnd.api+json`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'A successful document has the top-level members `data`, `links`, `meta` and `jsonapi`, with `jsonapi.version` equal to `"1.0"`, and `links.self` equal to the full URL of the request that produced it (query string included, exactly as received). `included` appears only when the request asked for it.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'A resource object has the members `type`, `id`, `attributes`, `relationships`, `links` and `meta`. Its `links.self` is the canonical single-resource URL for that record (e.g. `<base>/books/<id>`). The `attributes` object of a `book` contains exactly the keys `title`, `shelf`, `year`, `price_cents` and `restricted` — the primary key and any foreign key must never leak into `attributes`. An `author` exposes exactly `name` and `country`; a `review` exposes exactly `rating` and `body`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'On an `author` resource object, `relationships.books.links.related` must be `<base>/authors/<id>/books` and `relationships.books.links.self` must be `<base>/authors/<id>/relationships/books`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`GET /authors/:id/relationships/books` returns a `data` array whose entries are resource identifier objects carrying **only** the members `type` and `id`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Query features (index and single-resource GETs)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Sparse fieldsets** — `fields[<type>]=a,b` restricts the `attributes` of every resource of that type, in `data` and in `included` alike, to exactly the requested keys.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Inclusion** — `include=<path>[,<path>]`. `book` must support `author` and `reviews`; `author` must support `books` and the nested path `books.reviews`. Every relationship named by `include` must expose resource identifier linkage under `relationships.<name>.data` on the resources that own it, and `included` must contain every reachable related resource exactly once, with no duplicates.\n'[39m +

                [32m'* **Sorting** — `sort=<field>` and `sort=-<field>` (descending), comma-separated for multiple keys.\n'[39m +

When `page[count]=true` is also supplied, `meta.page.total` must be the total number of records matching the request, ignoring the page window.\n'[39m +

Successful creation answers `201`; successful fetch, update and deletion answer `200`.\n'[39m +

        {
          role: [32m'tool'[39m,
          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'Zqnlmej5Eone7XiC'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'readFile'[39m,
              output: {
                type: [32m'json'[39m,
                value: {
                  content: [32m'<!--\n'[39m +
                    [32m'SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2020 Zach Daniel\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n'[39m +
                    [32m'-->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Getting started with AshJsonApi\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Installing AshJsonApi\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<!-- tabs-open -->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using Igniter (recommended)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```sh\n'[39m +
                    [32m'mix igniter.install ash_json_api\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Manually\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This manual setup branches off from the [Getting Started with Ash](https://hexdocs.pm/ash/get-started.html) guide.\n'[39m +
                    [32m"If you aren't starting from there, replace the application name, `Helpdesk`, with your application name,\n"[39m +
                    [32m'and replace the `Ash.Domain` name, `Helpdesk.Support` with a domain or domains from your own application.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'#### Add the ash_json_api dependency\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'In your mix.exs, add the Ash JSON API dependency:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  defp deps do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      # .. other dependencies\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      {:ash_json_api, "~> 1.0"},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'#### Accept json_api content type\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Add the following to your `config/config.exs`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# config/config.exs\n'[39m +
                    [32m'config :mime,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  extensions: %{"json" => "application/vnd.api+json"},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  types: %{"application/vnd.api+json" => ["json"]}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This configuration is required to support working with the JSON:API custom mime type.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'After adding the configuration above, compiling the project might throw an error:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'ERROR! the application :mime has a different value set for key :types during runtime compared to compile time.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This can happen if `:mime` was already compiled before the configuration was changed and can be\n'[39m +
                    [32m'fixed by running\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'mix deps.compile mime --force\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'#### Create a router\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Create a separate Router Module to work with your Domains. It will generate the routes for\n'[39m +
                    [32m'your Resources and provide the functions you would usually have in a Controller.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'We will later forward requests from your Applications primary (Phoenix) Router to you Ash JSON API Router.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule HelpdeskWeb.JsonApiRouter do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use AshJsonApi.Router,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    # The api modules you want to serve\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    domains: [Helpdesk.Support],\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    # optionally an open_api route\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    open_api: "/open_api"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Additionally, your Resource requires a type, a base route and a set of allowed HTTP methods and what action they will trigger.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'#### Add `AshJsonApi.Plug.Parser` to your endpoint\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This handles any file uploads, if you have resource actions with the `:file` type.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'plug Plug.Parsers,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  parsers: [:urlencoded, :multipart, :json, AshJsonApi.Plug.Parser], # <- add it to this list.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  pass: ["*/*"],\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_decoder: Jason\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"You don't have to add this if you don't plan on doing any file uploads, but\n"[39m +
                    [32m"there is no cost to adding it, even if you don't use it.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'#### Add the routes from your domain module(s)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To make your Resources accessible to the outside world, forward requests from your Phoenix router to the router you created for your domains.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'scope "/api/json" do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  pipe_through(:api)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  forward "/helpdesk", HelpdeskWeb.JsonApiRouter\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<!-- tabs-close -->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Configure your Resources and Domain and expose actions\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'These examples are based off of the [Getting Started with Ash](https://hexdocs.pm/ash/get-started.html) guide.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Add the AshJsonApi extension to your domain and resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<!-- tabs-open -->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using Igniter (recommended)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To set up an existing resource of your own with `AshJsonApi`, run:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```sh\n'[39m +
                    [32m'mix ash.patch.extend Your.Resource.Name json_api\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Manually\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Add to your domain:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule Helpdesk.Support do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Domain, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Domain]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'And to your resource:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule Helpdesk.Support.Ticket do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Resource, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Resource]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    type "ticket"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<!-- tabs-close -->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Define Routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Routes can be defined on the resource or the domain. If you define them on the domain (which is our default recommendation), the resource in question must still use the `AshJsonApi.Resource` extension, and define its own type.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Defining routes on the domain\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule Helpdesk.Support do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Domain, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Domain]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      # in the domain `base_route` acts like a scope\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/tickets", Helpdesk.Support.Ticket do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        get :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :open\n'[39m +

          content: [
            {

              output: {
                type: [32m'json'[39m,
                value: {
                  content: [32m'<!--\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This file was generated by Spark. Do not edit it by hand.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'-->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Ash.Policy.Authorizer\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'An authorization extension for ash resources.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To add this extension to a resource, add it to the list of `authorizers` like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'use Ash.Resource,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ...,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  authorizers: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    Ash.Policy.Authorizer\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'A resource can be given a set of policies, which are enforced on each call to a resource action.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"For reads, policies can be configured to filter out data that the actor shouldn't see, as opposed to\n"[39m +
                    [32m'resulting in a forbidden error.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'See the [policies guide](/documentation/topics/security/policies.md) for practical examples.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Policies are solved/managed via a boolean satisfiability solver. To read more about boolean satisfiability,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'see this page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boolean_satisfiability_problem. At the end of\n'[39m +
                    [32m'the day, however, it is not necessary to understand exactly how Ash takes your\n'[39m +
                    [32m'authorization requirements and determines if a request is allowed. The\n'[39m +
                    [32m'important thing to understand is that Ash may or may not run any/all of your\n'[39m +
                    [32m'authorization rules as they may be deemed unnecessary. As such, authorization\n'[39m +
                    [32m'checks should have no side effects. Ideally, the checks built-in to ash should\n'[39m +
                    [32m'cover the bulk of your needs.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## policies\n'[39m +
                    [32m'A section for declaring authorization policies.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Each policy that applies must pass independently in order for the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'request to be authorized.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'See the [policies guide](/documentation/topics/security/policies.md) for more.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Nested DSLs\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [policy](#policies-policy)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * authorize_if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * forbid_if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * authorize_unless\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * forbid_unless\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [policy_group](#policies-policy_group)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * policy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * authorize_if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * forbid_if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * authorize_unless\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * forbid_unless\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [bypass](#policies-bypass)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * authorize_if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * forbid_if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * authorize_unless\n'[39m +
                    [32m'   * forbid_unless\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Examples\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'policies do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # Anything you can use in a condition, you can use in a check, and vice-versa\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # This policy applies if the actor is a super_user\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # Additionally, this policy is declared as a `bypass`. That means that this check is allowed to fail without\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # failing the whole request, and that if this check *passes*, the entire request passes.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  bypass actor_attribute_equals(:super_user, true) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    authorize_if always()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # This will likely be a common occurrence. Specifically, policies that apply to all read actions\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  policy action_type(:read) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    # unless the actor is an active user, forbid their request\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    forbid_unless actor_attribute_equals(:active, true)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    # if the record is marked as public, authorize the request\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    authorize_if attribute(:public, true)\n'[39m +
                    [32m"    # if the actor is related to the data via that data's `owner` relationship, authorize the request\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    authorize_if relates_to_actor_via(:owner)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Options\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| Name | Type | Default | Docs |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'|------|------|---------|------|\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| [`default_access_type`](#policies-default_access_type){: #policies-default_access_type } | `:strict \\| :filter \\| :runtime` | `:filter` | The default access type of policies for this resource. |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### policies.policy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'policy condition \\\\ nil\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'A policy has a name, a condition, and a list of checks.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Checks apply logically in the order they are specified, from top to bottom.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If no check explicitly authorizes the request, then the request is forbidden.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This means that, if you want to "blacklist" instead of "whitelist", you likely\n'[39m +
                    [32m'want to add an `authorize_if always()` at the bottom of your policy, like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'policy action_type(:read) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  forbid_if not_logged_in()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  forbid_if user_is_denylisted()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  forbid_if user_is_in_denylisted_group()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  authorize_if always()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If the policy should always run, use the `always()` check, like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'policy always() do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'See the [policies guide](/documentation/topics/security/policies.md) for more.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Nested DSLs\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [authorize_if](#policies-policy-authorize_if)\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [forbid_if](#policies-policy-forbid_if)\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [authorize_unless](#policies-policy-authorize_unless)\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [forbid_unless](#policies-policy-forbid_unless)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Arguments\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| Name | Type | Default | Docs |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'|------|------|---------|------|\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| [`condition`](#policies-policy-condition){: #policies-policy-condition } | `any` |  | A check or list of checks that must be true in order for this policy to apply. |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Options\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| Name | Type | Default | Docs |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'|------|------|---------|------|\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| [`description`](#policies-policy-description){: #policies-policy-description } | `String.t` |  | A description for the policy, used when explaining authorization results |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| [`access_type`](#policies-policy-access_type){: #policies-policy-access_type } | `:strict \\| :filter \\| :runtime` |  | Determines how the policy is applied. See the guide for more. |\n'[39m +
                    [32m"| [`error_message`](#policies-policy-error_message){: #policies-policy-error_message } | `String.t \\| (any, any -> any)` |  | A custom error message to surface when this policy is the reason a request is forbidden. Either a string, or a 2-arity function `(subject, context) -> String.t() \\| Exception.t()`. Returning an exception struct replaces the default `Ash.Error.Forbidden.Policy` entirely; returning a string sets the message on the default error. `subject` is the changeset/query/action input being authorized; `context` is a map of `:resource`, `:action`, `:actor`, `:domain`, and `:tenant`. Only takes effect when the policy is the one responsible for denying the request — the framework re-evaluates policies to identify which one failed and uses its `error_message`. If multiple policies contributed to the denial, the first one in source order whose state is `:forbidden` wins, falling back to the first whose state is `:unknown` (i.e. didn't authorize). |\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### policies.policy.authorize_if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'authorize_if check\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If the check is true, the request is authorized, otherwise run remaining checks.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Examples\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'authorize_if logged_in()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'authorize_if actor_attribute_matches_record(:group, :group)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Arguments\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| Name | Type | Default | Docs |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'|------|------|---------|------|\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| [`check`](#policies-policy-authorize_if-check){: #policies-policy-authorize_if-check .spark-required} | `any \\| module` |  | The check to run. See `Ash.Policy.Check` for more. |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Options\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| Name | Type | Default | Docs |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'|------|------|---------|------|\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| [`name`](#policies-policy-authorize_if-name){: #policies-policy-authorize_if-name } | `String.t` |  | A short name or description for the check, used when explaining authorization results |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Introspection\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Target: `Ash.Policy.Check`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### policies.policy.forbid_if\n'[39m +

                    [32m'forbid_if check\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +

                  content: [32m'<!--\n'[39m +

                    [32m'SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n'[39m +
                    [32m'-->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Relationships\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can specify which arguments will modify relationships using `relationship_arguments`, but there are some things to keep in mind.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`relationship_arguments` is a list of arguments that can be edited in the `data.relationships` input.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This is primarily useful for those who want to keep their relationship changes in compliance with the `JSON:API` spec.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If you are not focused on building a fully compliant JSON:API, it is likely far simpler to simply accept arguments\n'[39m +
                    [32m'in the `attributes` key and ignore the `data.relationships` input.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"If the argument's type is `{:array, _}`, a list of data will be expected. Otherwise, it will expect a single item.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Everything in this guide applies to routs defined on the domain as well.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# On a tweets resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# With a patch route that references the `authors` argument\n'[39m +
                    [32m'json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    patch :update, relationship_arguments: [:authors]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# And an argument by that name in the action\n'[39m +
                    [32m'actions do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  update :update do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    argument :authors, {:array, :map}, allow_nil?: false\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    change manage_relationship(:authors, type: :append_and_remove) # Use the authors argument to allow changing the related authors on update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can then send the value for `authors` in the relationships key, e.g\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                    [32m'{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  data: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    attributes: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    relationships: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      authors: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        data: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          {type: "author", id: 1}, // the `type` key is removed when the value is placed into the action, so this input would be `%{"id" => 1}` (`type` is required by `JSON:API` specification)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          {type: "author", id: 2, meta: {arbitrary: 1, keys: 2}}, <- `meta` is JSON:API spec freeform data, so this input would be `%{"id" => 2, "arbitrary" => 1, "keys" => 2}`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If you do not include `:authors` in the `relationship_arguments` key, you would supply its value in `attributes`, e.g:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  data: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    attributes: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      authors: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {id: 1},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {id: 2, arbitrary: 1, keys: 2},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Non-map argument types, e.g `argument :author, :integer` (expecting an author id) work with `manage_relationship`, but not with\n'[39m +
                    [32m'JSON:API, because it expects `{"type": _type, "id" => id}` for relationship values. To support non-map arguments in `relationship_arguments`,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'instead of `:author`, use `{:id, :author}`. This works for `{:array, _}` type arguments as well, so the value would be a list of ids.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Creating related resources without the id\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This feature is useful for creating relationships without requiring two separate API calls and without needing to associate resources with an ID first. This is an escape hatch from the standard approach and is not JSON:API spec compliant, but it is completely possible to implement.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# With a post route that references the `leads` argument, this will mean that\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# locations will have the ability to create Lead resources when called from \n'[39m +
                    [32m'# the API\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/location", Marketplace.Location do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create, relationship_arguments: [:leads]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/lead", Marketplace.Lead do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# In the leads resource you will have the following:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  actions do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    create :create do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      primary?(true)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      accept([:type, :description, :priority, :location_id])\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  relationships do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    belongs_to :location, Marketplace.Location\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# In the Location resource you will have the following:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  actions do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    create :create do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      primary?(true)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      accept([:name, :location, :images])\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      argument(:leads, {:array, :map}, allow_nil?: false)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      change(manage_relationship(:leads, type: :create))\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  relationships do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    has_many :leads, Marketplace.Lead\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This way, when requesting to create a location, leads will be automatically created as well.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                    [32m'{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  "data": {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    "type": "location",\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    "attributes": {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      "name": "Test Location",\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      "location": {\n'[39m +

                    [32m'      "images": ["url1", "url2", "url3"]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    "relationships": {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      "leads": {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        "data": [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            "type": "lead",\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            "meta": {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'              "type": "Roof",\n'[39m +

                    [32m'              "priority": "high"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            "type": "lead",\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            "meta": {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'              "type": "garden",\n'[39m +

                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"Note that the related data won't be returned unless included with the include query parameter. For the JSON:API specification on the include parameter, see [json api fetching includes](https://jsonapi.org/format/#fetching-includes).\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Relationship Manipulation Routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can also specify routes that are dedicated to manipulating relationships. We generally suggest the above approach, but JSON:API spec also allows for dedicated relationship routes. For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ...\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  # use `patch_relationship` when the operation is both additive and subtractive\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # use `delete_from_relationship` when the operation is subtractive\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This will use an action on the source resource, (by default the primary update), and expects it to take an argument with the corresponding name. Additionally, it must have a `change manage_relationship` that uses that attribute. For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'update :add_author do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  argument :author, :map\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  change manage_relationship(:author, type: :append)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
